source.title: On the Representations of Entities in Auto-regressive Large Language Models
source.authors: Victor Morand; Josiane Mothe; Benjamin Piwowarski

record.file_problem: No apparent text or document problem; the full paper, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study investigates decoding entity mentions from hidden representations, not whether a state represents tokens that occur later in the sequence or whether such a representation causally shapes intervening text. Its reconstruction results concern mentions that have already appeared.
record.gate_note: The paper trains task vectors to reconstruct previously occurring entity mentions from representations at the mention’s last token. This is a related but different direction of information flow from future-token look-ahead; the reconstruction results cannot establish the claim’s predicted behavior.
record.test_reason: The study decodes already-seen entity mentions from last-token hidden states with learned task vectors. It never measures information about tokens later in the sequence, rhyme planning, pre-caching, or look-ahead in other tasks. Future Lens (Pal et al., 2023) is cited only as a probing example in the Methodology section. Its decoding runs backward (past tokens), a related but different construct from V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that LLMs have entity-specific mechanisms: last-token states at middle layers suffice to recover frequent entities, while rarer ones are recovered by copying from context. They also find averaged or cleaned representations decode mentions better, and that entity representations support linear relation decoding. They draw no conclusion about planning or future tokens.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses learned task vectors to reconstruct past entity mentions; it does not apply the original look-ahead or rhyme-planning method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction performance differs between contextual and uncontextual decoding; the random-sequence contextual control varies by layer, with a reported maximum at layer 9.

fits_no_version.finding: In Phi-2, a learned task vector reconstructs a prior entity mention from its last-token state at 64% EM without context and 93% with context. A random 3-token control reaches 9% and at most 19% EM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hidden states encode preceding multi-token entity mentions (backward decodability), more so for frequent entities; this is not future-token look-ahead.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 8th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: The study does not measure future-token information or intervene on it to test effects on subsequent text. Its mention reconstruction uses a task vector trained specifically for reconstruction, and contextual decoding allows copying from the text. The reported uncertainty estimate for Figure 6 is described as small, but uncertainty for the cited exact-match values is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Other model curves and representation variants are shown in figures, but are not enumerated here because the plotted values are not stated numerically in the text and they concern entity-mention reconstruction rather than future-token look-ahead.

untested.parts: No rhyming verse, no frontier model, no intervention on a planned ending.
No decoding of tokens at positions after the hidden state; only preceding mention tokens are reconstructed.
No test of whether features are computed for later positions.
No rhyme planning in open models.
No look-ahead in reasoning, chess or Sokoban.
No test of the depth or causal use of future plans.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': Future Lens appears only as a citation about probes. The Entity Lens example where 'landmark' decodes to 'Eiffel Tower' is contextual inference about the current entity, not prediction of a future token.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming verse, candidate rhyme words, or intervention on a candidate ending.
No measurement of decoding tokens several positions after a hidden state; the study decodes entity mentions that precede the extracted last-token representation.
No test of pre-caching or features computed for later positions beyond next-token prediction.
No rhyme-planning test in open-weight models or attribution-graph/probing analysis of rhyme plans.
No look-ahead tests in reasoning, chess, Sokoban, or other tasks.
No test of whether apparent future plans are shallow, incidental, or causally unused.

rows.subject: Phi-2
rows.operation_detail: Decode the entity mention from its last-token representation using a learned task vector.
rows.measure: Exact match for reconstruction of the original entity mention
rows.note: This measures reconstruction of an entity mention that precedes the extracted representation, not prediction of future tokens or causal influence on intervening text.

rows.subject: Phi-2
rows.operation_detail: Decode the entity mention from its last-token representation using a learned task vector, with the original context available.
rows.measure: Exact match for reconstruction of the original entity mention
rows.note: The model can copy the already-present mention from context; this does not test future-token planning.

rows.subject: Phi-2
rows.operation_detail: Decode a randomly sampled three-token sequence from the representation of its final token using a newly learned task vector.
rows.baseline: Entity-mention decoding: 65% EM (reported as the comparison in Section 3.3)
rows.note: This is a control for entity-mention reconstruction specificity, not a future-token look-ahead control.
rows.check: Baseline says 65% EM, but the paper's own Phi-2 figure is 64% (Sec 3.3 and Table 2). The 65% is the paper's rounded figure for the best models.

rows.subject: Phi-2
rows.operation_detail: Decode a randomly sampled three-token sequence from the representation of its final token using a newly learned task vector, with the original context available.
rows.baseline: Entity-mention decoding: 93% EM (reported as the comparison in Section 3.3)
rows.note: The paper reports the control’s maximum at layer 9 and contrasts it with entity-mention reconstruction; neither measures the claim’s future-token behavior.
